title: sysdig: support the most recent version of sysdig
description: Update the pcap-ng reader and sysdig event dissector to support the second version of the sysdig event block, which was introduced after Wireshark's original implementation

notes.body:
Yes, I was thinking about how not nice this is as I was editing this code. 

Unfortunately, for reasons that I am still trying to figure out, around 3 years ago the SHB minor number in sysdig was bumped twice in a short amount of time. The result is that files produced by most of the sysdig versions currently around (and by other sysdig ecosystem tools like Falco) have the 1.2 number in them. I understand this is pretty annoying and makes those files essentially incompatible with a bunch of existing tooling, for no apparent good reason, but I thought at least I would make new versions of Wireshark able to open them.

If there is a better way to do this, I'm happy to entertain it. In the meatime I will try to figure out if the sysdig libraries can be reverted to produce compliant 1.0 files.

So in what fashion do 1.1 and 1.2 files differ from 1.0 files?

I.e., in what fashion would code that reads 1.0 files need to be changed to read 1.1 files (if there are any to read) and 1.2 files?

My understading is that they only difference is the presence of different blocks so, to answer your question, code that reads 1.0 should not require to be changed to read 1.1 and 1.2 files. In fact, adding support for 1.2 files in Wireshark didn't require any change other than adding support for V2 event blocks.

For reference, this the commit that bumped the number in sysdig:
https://github.com/falcosecurity/libs/commit/298fbde8029020ce3fbddd07e2910b59cc402b8b

So the commit comment said:

> Write the length of each fd list entry in the capture
> Instead of relying only on the whole block size, now each
> fd list entry have a length parameter.
> This allows older readers to skip new content if they
> don't know how to parse it.

and that change appears to have changed the block type for the fd list from `FDL_BLOCK_TYPE` to `FDL_BLOCK_TYPE_V2`, so that change wouldn't break any existing code that reads those blocks.

If that applies to the other changes, then we can just say code should treat V1.0, V1.1, and V1.2 identically.

One might say that the minor version change serves as a warning that there might be stuff in the file that can't be understood and will be discarded by the reader, but that's "might be", not "will be", unless the writer arranges to write out the newer minor version numbers if and *only* if there's new stuff, which means either knowing in advance what will be written or overwriting the version number at the end of the process.  If a program is writing a pcapng file to a pipe, overwriting the version number is impossible, so it'd have to know what's in the file before it starts writing.

Furthermore, reading existence of stuff that can't be understood and will be discarded also provides the same warning. :-)

OK, I've updated the spec to indicate that 1.2 should be treated like 1.0 when reading (but that programs shouldn't *write* 1.2 as a version number), and updated the main and 1.10-branch libpcap source to treat 1.2 like 1.0.

    /*
     * Minimum Sysdig event header size = minimum block size + packed size of sysdig_event_phdr.

    #define SYSDIG_EVENT_HEADER_SIZE ((16 + 64 + 64 + 32 + 16)/8) /* CPU ID + TS + TID + Event len + Event type */

    #define SYSDIG_EVENT_V2_HEADER_SIZE ((16 + 64 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 32)/8) /* CPU ID + TS + TID + Event len + Event type + nparams */

- parse the number of system call arguments in a way that works for both V1 and V2 event blocks
- returned the correct error string when unable to read the nparams entry from a sysdig event block V2
